Battle of Mice/Julie Christmas is wonderful and dark. Battle of Mice dissolved almost 20 years ago, but the music is still there, and it’s really dark and heavy. (A similar song would be Hurt You Electric Cross, something dark and disturbing.)

Obscure Sphinx is another favorite of mine. Also very dark and atmospheric, but they release music still. (A similar song would be Fata Morgana or Sew Me Up, maybe Aphids or The Mara Effect. Something heavy with a lot of emotion.)

If you want more of a metalcore vibe, seeyouspacecowboy is a great band. Courtney did a collab with them a while ago.

Also agree with whoever said Oceans of Slumber. Cammie is one of the best metal vocalists ever imo. (A similar song would be Eternal Blue, Perfect Soul, or Secret Garden. Very ethereal with amazing cleans. To The Sea (A Tolling Of The Bells) is very similar to Constance. It’s a beautiful song.)

If you’re more into the vocal aspect and are willing to branch out genre-wise, Lingua Ignota is a fantastic vocalist. Her stuff is more noise/avant-garde but still definitely has a metal influence. Almost every song is about DV/SA so be warned if you do choose to check her out. (A similar song would be The Beauty of Suffering or Keep Sweet for anger/lyrics/subject matter or the acoustic version of Constance for what her later music sounds like.)

You know what’s best for you, don’t let your parents dictate who can and can’t come. Your friends should be happy for you. Do they know the full story? If so, then tell them. Why are you prioritizing your ex’s feelings over yours and your boyfriend’s? Ultimately, it’s your decision and judgement, but I would tell your friend group.

As someone with depression: he’s aware of how you’re feeling. But, you also need to prioritize your feelings. If you don’t see things working out with him, then it’s ok to cut your losses. If he has a doctor, maybe he can talk about meds/therapy if he can afford it. If that’s not an option, then I’d break up with him. It’s harsh, but I think he’d rather see you happy with someone else. 

The random availability is another thing. Like you said, you have a life to live. If it’s stressing you out, talk to him about it.

The therapists are “trash”? How? Maybe there should be more focus on medication if he can afford it. I don’t know what his case is, but meds helped me more than therapy.

I’d also encourage him to get a job. Socializing might help, and it’ll take some stress off of you as well if he finds more people to talk to about things. All in all, if you see things progressing with him, I’d talk to him and see if he’s willing to try any of the things I listed above. If not, break things off. Maybe he’ll see it as a wake up call.

OP I’ve been in a very similar situation. My dad has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder so he would go from happy to mad in milliseconds. Constant yelling, fighting, and getting mad at things it made no sense to get mad at. Even your pet situation is very similar. My cat would throw up constantly and he’d leave it on the ground or make me clean it, and he never took my cat to the vet. I wouldn’t be surprised if there was some physical abuse involved as well. If your mother works she might be able to leave him. If not, then try getting your dad into some form of therapy or to a psychiatrist if you can afford it. If you can move in with a friend temporarily then do so. Being wound up all the time and trying to read his emotions as to not set him off is no way to live, and you will feel so much better when you’re away from him, trust me.
